name: CORRECTION: the published attention resource numbers were for a design with NO KV cache
status: MEASURED (resources); the corrected RTL is VERIFIED; the throughput probe does not route in openXC7
why_this_iteration_exists: Building the first throughput probe on a design with a running clock forced the attention module to be instantiated in a new context. The probe's counter never advanced past its first value, which exposed that the committed attention module's KV cache was not actually present in the synthesized netlist.

defects_found.detail: the cache was declared `reg [QUANT_W-1:0] kv_kmag [0:HEAD_DIM-1];` - ONE dimension - and indexed `kv_kmag[c][slot_ptr]`, a bit-select out of range on an 8-bit value
defects_found.evidence: the committed module synthesises to 145 LCs and 279 FFs at HEAD_DIM=2/KV_LEN=16 with NO cache; the corrected module has 6 RAMB18E1 or 18 RAM32M or 999 FFs
defects_found.consequence: every published attention resource number was for a design with NO KV cache

defects_found.detail: a flat packed vector written with a VARIABLE-OFFSET part-select is not synthesizable as a register file: yosys drops the write, the cache reads as constant, and the memory is pruned - while the SIMULATION still passes
defects_found.evidence: the corrected module in the flat-vector form still synthesised to 333 FFs with no cache until the cache was changed to a MEMORY
defects_found.lesson: a design can be correct in simulation and dead in synthesis; only the netlist tells the truth

defects_found.detail: the key magnitude was padded as {1'b0, magnitude, 1'b0}, a factor of 16, and multiplied by a separate +/-1 weight, so the 17-bit score accumulator overflowed and the score's SIGN - which selects add versus subtract - was wrong
defects_found.evidence: the Verilog golden testbench mismatched on 40/40 trials of the committed module

defects_found.detail: the key magnitude was held in a QUANT_W-bit SIGNED register, so any magnitude >= 2^(QUANT_W-1) came out negative before the stored sign was applied

the accumulator addition was `out_next[c*16 +: 16] + vq_ext`, and a Verilog part-select is ALWAYS UNSIGNED, so a negative value contribution was added as a large unsigned number (-240 became 272, and eight slots gave 2176 instead of -1920)
defects_found.evidence: the DUT produced exactly 2176 where the golden produced -1920

corrected_resource_numbers.note: yosys 0.67+post synth_xilinx -family xc7 -nodsp -nosrl -flatten. THREE cache implementations are valid, and which one is used is a real co-design choice.

distributed_ram_LUTRAM.description: the cache is a memory and yosys infers distributed RAM (RAM32M); zero block RAM

block_ram.description: the cache is a memory and yosys infers block RAM (RAMB18E1); -nolutram

registers.description: the cache is a flat packed vector, so it becomes flip-flops and a mux; no RAM primitive at all

corrected_resource_numbers.co_design_finding: The cache IMPLEMENTATION is a first-class decision: distributed RAM costs 2763 LCs and zero BRAM, block RAM costs 2934 LCs and 6 RAMB18E1 (0.8% of the 730 available), and registers cost 18695 LCs and no RAM at all. The register form is the only one that does NOT fit the 10% cap.

resource_cap_consequence.verdict: with a memory-based cache the adopted HEAD_DIM=8 / KV_LEN=16 configuration FITS the 10% cap comfortably - 2763 LCs (2.05%) distributed RAM or 2934 LCs (2.17%) with 6 block RAMs. The earlier 'it does not fit' verdict came from the register-cache form alone.

what_survives: the QUALITY RULE, QUANT_W >= ACT_BITS for losslessness: it was derived from an exact simulation of the EQUATIONS, which the defects did not change
the sequential-vs-combinational ORDERING: the combinational form computes all SLOTS in parallel and therefore needs SLOTS times more score logic, so it is still the worse form
the cycle structure, SLOTS + 2 cycles per token: it is a property of the control machine, not of the arithmetic
every resource number for designs whose cache was never involved - the MAC probe, the utilisation report
what_is_withdrawn: the token-sequential attention's resource numbers (505 LCs, 345 FFs) - they were for a cache-less design
the claim that every configuration fits inside the 10% resource cap - the adopted HEAD_DIM=8 configuration does not
the 'ACCEPT act_bits=4, quant_w=4' decision at the adopted HEAD_DIM, to the extent it rested on the cache-less numbers
the BRAM = 0 statement, for the attention: the corrected cache is registers at these sizes, but that is now a measured statement about a different design

verification_state_of_the_corrected_rtl.method: Verilator, which enforces the semantics a synthesizer sees; a CPU golden computed from the same cache contents
verification_state_of_the_corrected_rtl.why_verilator_not_icarus: Icarus ACCEPTED the variable-offset part-select write that yosys silently drops, so a module could pass in Icarus and be dead in the netlist. Verilator rejects it.
verification_state_of_the_corrected_rtl.coverage: 10 configurations (HEAD_DIM x KV_LEN: 1x1, 1x4, 1x8, 1x16, 2x8, 2x16, 4x8, 4x16, 8x8, 8x16), 120 randomised trials each = 1200 trials
golden_side_bugs_found_and_fixed: a Verilog part-select of q is always UNSIGNED, so the golden multiplied an unsigned activation byte by a signed score; the DUT used $signed(q[...]) and was right
the golden ignored the value's stored sign
the golden started the comparison while the fill token's done pulse was still high
verification_state_of_the_corrected_rtl.honest_note: the testbench found five real defects in the RTL under test and three in the golden itself. Each one produced plausible-looking numbers that were wrong, which is why the test runs against an independent golden under a simulator that enforces synthesis semantics.

decision: PUBLISH THE CORRECTED, VERIFIED RTL AND ITS TRUE RESOURCE NUMBERS WITH THE THREE CACHE IMPLEMENTATIONS; the throughput number remains unpublished because the probe does not route in openXC7
decision_rationale: The published numbers are wrong by about 37x in flip-flops, and leaving them up would be a false claim in the portfolio's headline section.
The correction itself is a measured result: the corrected resource numbers come from the same synthesis flow as the original ones.
The throughput measurement depends on this module, so it waits until the module is verified rather than shipping a number from an unverified design.
next_iteration: obtain a working flow for a memory-based design: Vivado, a patched nextpnr, or a reduced probe small enough to route
then measure the first throughput number on the verified module and publish it with its uncertainty

throughput_attempt.status: ATTEMPTED - the probe does not route in openXC7
throughput_attempt.probe: evidence/attention_fix/token_rate_probe.v - the VERIFIED attention at HEAD_DIM=2, KV_LEN=16, clocked from the R4/T4 200 MHz oscillator, with a 20-bit token counter read over BSCANE2 and an LED on B13

routing_attempts.error: No wire found for port A6 on destination cell - the BRAM's address input
No wire found for port DI2 on destination cell u_attn.kv_vword.0.0/DPR2_1 - the LUTRAM's data input
Failed to route arc 0 of net 'sr[28]' - the BSCANE2 shift register scattered by the placer

throughput_attempt.diagnosis: openXC7's RAM packer cannot wire a memory's ports in this design, and its placer scatters the BSCANE2 shift register when the design is large enough to give it room to do so. The BSCANE2-only clock probes route; the attention does not.
throughput_attempt.an_important_subtlety_found: the probe's token counter counts `done`, which depends only on the CONTROL machine. If the LED showed only the counter, the attention's data path would be unobservable and synthesis would prune the arithmetic and the cache away - the probe would look absurdly small and would measure nothing. Making the LED carry the attention's output keeps the data path alive.
throughput_attempt.what_is_needed: a working Xilinx flow for a design with a memory-based KV cache: Vivado (AMD account), or a patched nextpnr, or a design small enough for the placer not to scatter the shift register
